cohort: The study included births at two San Francisco hospitals (a safety net hospital and an academic medical center) during specific periods in 2019 and 2020.
finding: In San Francisco, the COVID-19 lockdown period from August to December 2020 was associated with a decreased preterm birth rate, overall longer gestational duration, and greater birthweight compared to the same period in 2019.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences found in the type of delivery (vaginal versus Cesarean section) between the lockdown period and the prior year.
cross-section timing: Births from March to May 2019 and 2020, and August to December 2019 and 2020.
birth_weight: Low birthweight was defined as < 2500 g; the study found an association with greater birthweight (Coeff 43.76g).
gest_age: Preterm birth was defined as < 37 weeks; the study found an association with overall longer gestational duration (Coeff 0.23 weeks).
